mishnayos.summary: A maiden gets married on Wednesday and a widow on Thursday. This is because the batei din sat on Mondays and Thursdays, so a chasan with a complaint could go to beis din right away.

chunks.en: A maiden gets married on Wednesday,

words.note: A girl who was never married before.

chunks.en: and a widow on Thursday.

chunks.he: שֶׁפַּעֲמַיִם בַּשַּׁבָּת בָּתֵּי דִינִין יוֹשְׁבִין בָּעֲיָרוֹת,
chunks.en: Because twice a week the batei din sit in the towns,

words.note: Batei din are Jewish courts.

chunks.en: on Monday and on Thursday.
So if the chasan has a complaint that she was not really a maiden,
he can go early the next morning to the beis din.

mishnayos.summary: A maiden's kesubah is two hundred zuz, and a widow's is one hundred. A woman whose first marriage ended before the chuppah, or who became Jewish or was freed while very little, still counts as a maiden.

chunks.en: A maiden's kesubah is two hundred zuz,

words.note: The marriage contract: money promised to the wife if the marriage ends.

chunks.en: and a widow's is one hundred.
A maiden who became a widow,
or was divorced, or had chalitzah,

words.note: A widow freed by chalitzah from marrying her husband's brother.

chunks.en: after only the erusin,

words.note: The first step of marriage, before the chuppah.

chunks.en: their kesubah is two hundred zuz,
and the husband can complain if she was not a maiden.
A woman who became a giyores, or a captive woman,
or a maidservant, who were ransomed or became Jewish

chunks.he: וְשֶׁנִּשְׁתַּחְרְרוּ, פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: or were set free when they were younger than three years and one day,
their kesubah is two hundred zuz,
and the husband can complain if she was not a maiden.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir says that a girl who was hurt in certain ways still counts as a maiden, with a kesubah of two hundred. The Sages say a girl hurt by a piece of wood gets only one hundred.

chunks.en: A little girl who was harmed by a grown man,
or a grown woman who was with a young boy,
or a girl who was hurt by a piece of wood,
chunks.explain: An accident made her no longer seem like a maiden.

chunks.en: their kesubah is two hundred zuz.
That is what Rabbi Meir says.
But the Sages say,
a girl hurt by a piece of wood gets a kesubah of one hundred.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who was a widow or divorced after a full marriage gets a kesubah of one hundred, even if she is really still a maiden. The same is true for a giyores, captive or freed maidservant who was older than three.

chunks.en: A maiden who became a widow,
or was divorced, or had chalitzah,
after a full marriage (the chuppah),
her kesubah is one hundred,
and the husband cannot complain that she was not a maiden.
A giyores, or a captive woman,
or a maidservant, who were ransomed,
or became Jewish, or were set free,

chunks.he: יְתֵרוֹת עַל בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: when they were older than three years and one day,
their kesubah is one hundred,
and the husband cannot complain that she was not a maiden.

mishnayos.summary: In Yehudah a chasan could be alone with his kallah before the wedding, so he cannot complain later. The mishnah also teaches about a Kohen's daughter's kesubah.

chunks.he: הָאוֹכֵל אֵצֶל חָמִיו בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁלֹּא בְעֵדִים,
chunks.en: A man who eats at his father-in-law's house in Yehudah, with no witnesses watching,
cannot complain that she was not a maiden,
because he was alone with her.

chunks.he: אַחַת אַלְמְנַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַת אַלְמְנַת כֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: Both a regular widow and a Kohen's widow
have a kesubah of one hundred.
A beis din of Kohanim would
collect four hundred zuz for a maiden (a Kohen's daughter),
and the Sages did not stop them.

mishnayos.summary: A chasan says his kallah was not a maiden before the erusin, and she says something happened only after the erusin. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer believe her; Rabbi Yehoshua says she needs proof.

chunks.he: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וְלֹא מָצָא לָהּ בְּתוּלִים,
chunks.en: If a man marries a woman and finds that she is not a maiden,
she says,
Something bad happened to me after you made me your kallah,
so it is your bad luck.
chunks.explain: A saying: the bad luck fell on you.

chunks.en: And he says,
No,
it happened before I engaged you,
so my deal was a mistake.
Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say,
She is believed. Rabbi Yehoshua says,
We do not live by what she says.
Rather, we treat her as
someone who was not a maiden before the erusin
who fooled him, until she brings proof for her words.

mishnayos.summary: A kallah says she was hurt by a piece of wood, and the chasan says a man harmed her. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer believe her; Rabbi Yehoshua says she needs proof.

chunks.en: She says, I was hurt by a piece of wood,
and he says,
No,
rather, a man harmed you.
Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say,
She is believed. And Rabbi Yehoshua says,
We do not live by what she says.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא הֲרֵי זוֹ בְחֶזְקַת דְּרוּסַת אִישׁ,
chunks.en: Rather, we treat her as someone harmed by a man,
until she brings proof for her words.

mishnayos.summary: A woman was seen with a man people did not know, and she says he is a kosher Kohen. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer believe her, so she may still marry a Kohen; Rabbi Yehoshua says she needs proof.

chunks.en: People saw her talking with a man in the market.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לָהּ מַה טִּיבוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
chunks.en: They asked her, Who is this man?
She said, He is a certain man, and he is a Kohen.
Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say,
She is believed. And Rabbi Yehoshua says,
We do not live by what she says.
Rather, we treat her as
someone who was with a nasin or a mamzer,
chunks.explain: Then she may not marry a Kohen.

words.note: From the Givonim, who may not marry into the Jewish people.
A child of a forbidden relationship, who may not marry most Jews.

chunks.en: until she brings proof for her words.

mishnayos.summary: An unmarried woman is expecting a baby and says the father is a kosher Kohen. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer believe her; Rabbi Yehoshua says she needs proof.

chunks.en: An unmarried woman was expecting a baby,
and people asked her, What kind
of father does this baby have?
She said, From a certain man, and he is a Kohen.
Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say,
She is believed. Rabbi Yehoshua says,
We do not live by what she says.
Rather, we treat her as
having a baby from a nasin or a mamzer,
until she brings proof for her words.

mishnayos.summary: A girl was harmed by a stranger at the spring. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says that if most of the town's people may marry Kohanim, she may marry a Kohen too.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
Once a young girl went down to fill
water from the spring,

chunks.he: וְנֶאֱנְסָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי,
chunks.en: and someone harmed her. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said,

chunks.he: אִם רֹב אַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר מַשִּׂיאִין לַכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: If most people of the town marry their daughters to Kohanim,
this girl may marry a Kohen.

mishnayos.summary: A widow or divorced woman says she married as a maiden, and her husband says she was a widow. If witnesses saw her wedding done the way maidens' weddings were done, she gets two hundred.

chunks.en: A woman who became a widow or was divorced,
chunks.st: a woman who was widowed or divorced,
chunks.stMore: and is now claiming payment of her marriage contract that is not before the court,

chunks.en: she says, You married me as a maiden,
chunks.st: and she says: You married me as a virgin, who is entitled to two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and he says,
chunks.st: and he says:

chunks.en: No, I married you as a widow.
chunks.st: No; rather, I married you as a widow, who is entitled to one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: If there are witnesses that she went out to her wedding
chunks.st: then, if there are witnesses that she went out of her father’s house to her wedding

chunks.en: with a hinuma and with her hair loose,
chunks.explain: This was how maidens went to their wedding.
chunks.st: with a hinnuma or with her hair uncovered, in a manner typical of virgins,

words.note: A special canopy or veil for a kallah who was a maiden.

chunks.en: her kesubah is two hundred.
chunks.st: payment of her marriage contract is two hundred dinars.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

chunks.en: Even handing out roasted grain is a proof.
chunks.explain: In his town they did this at a maiden's wedding.
chunks.st: Even testimony that there was distribution of roasted grain, which was customary at weddings of virgins, constitutes proof that she is a virgin.

mishnayos.summary: If someone says, This field was your father's and I bought it from him, he is believed, because the same mouth that made the problem also took it away. But if there are witnesses it was the father's, he is not believed.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ שָׂדֶה
chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua agrees about a man who tells his friend, This field
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes in a case where one says to another: This field, which is currently in my possession,

chunks.he: זוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיךָ הָיְתָה וּלְקַחְתִּיהָ הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: was your father's, and I bought it from him,
chunks.st: belonged to your father and I purchased it from him,

chunks.en: that he is believed,
chunks.st: that he is deemed credible,
chunks.stMore: and his entire claim is accepted. The court accepts not only his admission that it once belonged to the other’s father, but also his statement that he purchased it.

chunks.en: because the mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it allowed.
chunks.explain: Without his words, we would not know it was the father's.
chunks.st: This is so, as the mouth that prohibited, i.e., claimed that the field had belonged to the other’s father, is the mouth that permitted,
chunks.stMore: i.e., claimed that he purchased the field. Even if he had not admitted that it had belonged to the other’s father, the field would have remained in his possession. Therefore, his claim is accepted.

chunks.en: But if there are witnesses that it belonged
chunks.st: However, if there are witnesses that the field belonged to

chunks.en: to his father, and he says, I bought it from him,
chunks.st: his father, and the one who has the field in his possession says: I purchased it from him,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: he is not deemed credible and his claim is rejected.

mishnayos.stIntro: Several disputes between Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua were cited previously with regard to the credibility accorded to the respective claims of parties to a dispute. Based on one of those disputes, the tanna adds:

mishnayos.summary: Witnesses who say, This is our signature, but we were forced, or too young, or not kosher witnesses, are believed. But if their signatures can be proven without them, they are not believed.

chunks.he: הָעֵדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתַב יָדֵינוּ הוּא זֶה,
chunks.en: Witnesses who said, This is our handwriting,
chunks.st: the witnesses who said in their testimony to ratify their signatures in a document: We signed the document and this is our handwriting;

chunks.en: but we were forced to sign,
chunks.st: however, we were compelled to sign, or

chunks.en: we were children,
chunks.st: we were minors when we signed, or

chunks.en: we were not allowed to be witnesses,
chunks.st: we were disqualified witnesses, e.g., we are relatives of one of the parties,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: they are deemed credible.
chunks.stMore: Since the document is ratified on the basis of their testimony, it is likewise invalidated on the basis of their testimony.

chunks.en: But if there are other witnesses that it is their
chunks.st: However, if there are other witnesses who testify

chunks.en: handwriting, or their handwriting
chunks.st: that it is their handwriting, or if their handwriting

chunks.en: shows up on a paper from another place,
chunks.st: emerges on a document from another place,
chunks.stMore: enabling confirmation of their signatures by comparing the two documents,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: then the witnesses who signed the document are not deemed credible.
chunks.stMore: The document is not invalidated based on their testimony, because ratification of the document is not dependent on their testimony, as their signatures can be authenticated independently.

mishnayos.summary: Two witnesses can prove that their signatures on a document are real. Rebbi says each one must also be backed up by another person; the Sages say each man is believed about his own signature.

chunks.en: One says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: this witness whose name is signed on a document says: This is my handwriting

chunks.en: and this is my friend's handwriting,
chunks.st: and this is the handwriting of my fellow witness,

chunks.en: and the other says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: and that witness says: This is my handwriting

chunks.en: and this is my friend's handwriting,
chunks.st: and that is the handwriting of my fellow witness,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: these witnesses are deemed credible
chunks.stMore: and the document is ratified, as together they provide testimony authenticating both signatures.

chunks.en: If one says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: If this witness says: This is my handwriting,

chunks.en: and the other says, This is my handwriting,
chunks.st: and that witness says: This is my handwriting,
chunks.stMore: and neither testifies with regard to the signature of the other,

chunks.en: they need another person to join them.
chunks.st: they must add another witness with them
chunks.stMore: who will authenticate the signatures of the two witnesses, as otherwise, each of the witnesses would be testifying with regard to half the sum in the document;

chunks.en: That is what Rebbi says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they do not need another person to join them.
chunks.st: They need not add another witness with them.

chunks.en: Rather, a person is believed to say,
chunks.st: Rather, a person is deemed credible to say:

chunks.en: This is my handwriting.
chunks.st: This is my handwriting.
chunks.stMore: The testimony of the two signatories about their own signatures is sufficient.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who says, I was married and now I am divorced, is believed, because without her words we would not know she was married. The same is true for a woman who says she was taken captive but stayed pure.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמְרָה אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ הָיִיתִי וּגְרוּשָׁה אָנִי,
chunks.en: A woman who said, I was a married woman and now I am divorced,

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
chunks.en: is believed, because the mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it allowed.
But if there are witnesses that she was a married
woman, and she says, I am divorced,
she is not believed.
If she said, I was taken captive, but I am pure,
chunks.explain: Pure here means nothing bad happened to her.

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
chunks.en: she is believed, because the mouth that made it forbidden is the mouth that made it allowed.
But if there are witnesses that she was taken captive,
and she says, I am pure,
she is not believed.
But if the witnesses came after she got married,
she does not have to leave her husband.

mishnayos.summary: Two women who were taken captive cannot each say about herself that she stayed pure. But each one may speak up for the other.

chunks.en: Two women were taken captive.
chunks.st: two women who were taken captive, and

chunks.en: This one says, I was taken captive, but I am pure,
chunks.st: this woman says: I was taken captive but I am pure,

chunks.en: and that one says, I was taken captive, but I am pure.
chunks.st: and that woman says: I was taken captive but I am pure,

chunks.en: They are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְעִידוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
chunks.en: But when each one speaks up for the other,
chunks.st: And when this woman testifies about that woman that she is pure and vice versa,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: they are deemed credible.

chunks.en: And the same with two men:
chunks.st: And likewise, with regard to two men whose lineage is unknown, and

chunks.en: this one says, I am a Kohen,
chunks.st: this man says: I am a priest,

chunks.en: and that one says, I am a Kohen.
chunks.st: and that man says: I am a priest,

chunks.en: They are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְעִידִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
chunks.en: But when each one speaks up for the other,
chunks.st: And when this man testifies about that man that he is a priest and vice versa,

chunks.en: they are believed.
chunks.st: they are deemed credible.

mishnayos.summary: Can one witness make a man a Kohen? Rabbi Yehudah says no. Rabbi Elazar says that one witness is enough if nobody argues, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says one witness is enough.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: We do not raise a man up to be a Kohen
chunks.st: One does not elevate a man to priesthood

chunks.en: because of one witness.
chunks.st: on the basis of one witness. Two witnesses are required for that purpose.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: When is that? Where there are people who argue.
chunks.st: When is that the ruling? In a case where there are challengers to his claim that he is a priest.

chunks.en: But where nobody argues,
chunks.st: However, in a case where there are no challengers,

chunks.he: מַעֲלִין לַכְּהֻנָּה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
chunks.en: we raise him up to be a Kohen because of one witness.
chunks.st: one elevates a man to priesthood on the basis of one witness.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says

chunks.en: in the name of Rabbi Shimon, the son of the Segan,
chunks.st: in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy High Priest:

words.note: The helper of the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.he: מַעֲלִין לַכְּהֻנָּה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד:
chunks.en: We raise him up to be a Kohen because of one witness.
chunks.st: One elevates a man to priesthood on the basis of one witness.

mishnayos.summary: A woman held by goyim may sometimes not stay married to her Kohen husband, because we worry something bad was done to her. Witnesses can help her, but a husband cannot speak up for his own wife.

chunks.en: A woman who was locked up by goyim
because of money (a debt),
may stay with her husband.
If it was because of a crime punished by death,
she may not stay with her husband.
chunks.explain: We worry something bad was done to her.

chunks.en: When an army takes over a city,
all wives of Kohanim found inside it
may not stay with their husbands. But if they have witnesses,
even a slave,
even a maidservant,
they are believed.

chunks.he: וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן אָדָם עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
chunks.en: But a person is not believed about himself.
Rabbi Zecharyah ben HaKatzav said,
I swear by this Beis HaMikdash,

chunks.he: לֹא זָזָה יָדָהּ מִתּוֹךְ יָדִי מִשָּׁעָה
chunks.en: her hand did not leave my hand from the time
the goyim came into Yerushalayim until they left.
They said to him,

chunks.he: אֵין אָדָם מֵעִיד עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ:
chunks.en: A person cannot testify about himself.

mishnayos.summary: Grown-ups are believed about some things they saw when they were children, like whose handwriting this is, or that someone was a Kohen. But they are not believed when it would take land away from someone.

chunks.en: These may testify when they are grown up
chunks.st: And these are deemed credible to testify in their majority with regard to

chunks.en: about what they saw when they were young:
chunks.st: what they saw in their minority.

chunks.en: A person is believed to say,
chunks.st: A person is deemed credible to say:

chunks.en: This is my father's handwriting,
chunks.st: This is my father’s handwriting, and to say:

chunks.en: and this is my rebbi's handwriting,
chunks.st: This is my teacher’s handwriting; and to say:

chunks.en: and this is my brother's handwriting.
chunks.st: This is my brother’s handwriting,

chunks.en: I remember that a certain woman went out with a hinuma
chunks.st: Similarly, one is deemed credible to say: I was reminded of the wedding of so-and-so, who went out with a hinnuma,

chunks.en: and with her hair loose.
chunks.explain: So she married as a maiden.
chunks.st: or with her hair uncovered
chunks.stMore: in a manner typical of virgins, and therefore, her marriage contract is two hundred dinars;

chunks.en: And that a certain man used to leave school
chunks.st: and to say that so-and-so would leave school

chunks.en: to toivel so he could eat terumah.
chunks.explain: So he must be a Kohen.
chunks.st: to immerse in order to partake of teruma,

chunks.en: And that he took a share with us at the threshing floor.
chunks.st: and that he would share teruma with us at the threshing floor

chunks.st: This place is a beit haperas, a field with a grave that was plowed, scattering the bones, and rendering the field a place of uncertain ritual impurity; and to say:

chunks.en: And that we used to walk until here on Shabbos.
chunks.st: Until here we would come on Shabbat and thereby determine the Shabbat boundary.

chunks.en: But a person is not believed to say,
chunks.st: However, a person is neither deemed credible to say:

chunks.en: So-and-so had a path in this place,
chunks.st: So-and-so had a path in this place;

chunks.he: מַעֲמָד וּמִסְפֵּד הָיָה לִפְלוֹנִי בַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה:
chunks.en: or, So-and-so had a place for standing and for eulogies here.
chunks.st: nor to say: So-and-so had a tract of land where they would perform the ritual of standing and sitting and deliver a eulogy in that place,
chunks.stMore: thereby attesting that the land belongs to that person. The reason he is not deemed credible in those cases is that full-fledged testimony is required to remove property from the possession of its presumptive owner.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah sets a fine (kenas) that a man must pay when he harms a young girl. This mishnah lists girls who get the fine even though they were forbidden to him.

chunks.en: These are the girls who get a kenas (fine):

words.note: A fine the Torah sets for a man who harms a young girl.

chunks.en: And these girls do not get a kenas:

Rabbi Akiva says,

mishnayos.summary: A man who tricked a girl pays three kinds of payment, and one who forced her pays four. The mishnah lists the differences between them.

chunks.en: The one who tricks a girl pays three things,
and the one who forces her pays four.
The one who tricks pays for shame, for damage, and the kenas.
The one who forces adds to that,
that he pays for the pain.
What is the difference between them?
The one who forces pays for the pain,
and the one who tricks does not pay for the pain.
The one who forces pays right away,
and the one who tricks pays only if he sends her away.
The one who forces must drink from his own pot,
chunks.explain: He must marry her and may never send her away.

chunks.en: and the one who tricks may send her away if he wants.

mishnayos.summary: The one who forced a girl must marry her and keep her, even if she has a handicap. But if she is forbidden to him, he may not stay married to her.

Even if she is lame,
even if she is blind,
and even if she has boils, he must keep her.
But if she did a forbidden thing,
or she is not allowed to marry a Jew,
he may not keep her,
as it says (Devarim 22), And she shall be his wife,
a wife who is fit for him.

mishnayos.summary: An orphan girl had erusin and was divorced. Rabbi Elazar says that one who tricked her does not pay the kenas, but one who forced her does.

chunks.en: Anyone who gives a maiden less than two hundred, or a widow less than one hundred,

mishnayos.summary: After the erusin, a maiden gets twelve months to get ready for the wedding, and a widow thirty days. If the time came and the chasan did not marry her, he must feed her, and a Kohen may feed her terumah.

chunks.en: We give a maiden twelve months
from when the chasan asks for her, to get herself ready.

chunks.en: so we give the man time to get himself ready.
And a widow gets thirty days.
If the time came and they did not get married,
she eats from his food, and she eats terumah.
chunks.explain: If the chasan is a Kohen.

We may give her all of it as terumah.
Rabbi Akiva says,
Half regular food and half terumah.

mishnayos.summary: If a man makes his wife's work hekdesh, it does not work, and she keeps working and eating from it. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar argue about her extra earnings.

chunks.en: One who makes his wife's work hekdesh,
chunks.st: If one consecrates his wife’s earnings,

chunks.en: she keeps working and eating from it.
chunks.st: she may work and sustain

chunks.en: About the extra, Rabbi Meir says,

mishnayos.summary: A wife does certain jobs in the house, and the more maidservants she brings with her, the fewer jobs she must do. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teach that a person should not sit doing nothing.

chunks.en: These are jobs a wife does for her husband:
she grinds flour, and bakes,
and washes clothes, cooks,
and feeds her baby,
makes his bed,
and spins wool.
If she brought him one maidservant,
she does not grind,
and does not bake and does not wash clothes.

chunks.he: שְׁתַּיִם, אֵינָהּ מְבַשֶּׁלֶת וְאֵינָהּ מֵנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ.
chunks.en: Two maidservants: she does not cook and does not nurse her baby.
Three: she does not make his bed
and does not spin wool.
Four: she sits in a fancy chair.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
even if she brought him a hundred maidservants,
he makes her spin wool,
because doing nothing leads to bad behavior.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,

chunks.he: אַף הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה,

for thirty days.
Workers, one week.
The set times written in the Torah:

Donkey drivers: once a week.
Camel drivers: once in thirty days.
Sailors: once in six months.
That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.

chunks.en: A wife who rebels against her husband:

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: we add three dinars a week to her kesubah.
chunks.st: three dinars a week are added to her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: three half-dinars.
chunks.st: Three terapa’ikin.

chunks.st: he may not give her less than two kav of wheat

chunks.st: or four kav of barley a week for her sustenance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.st: Only

chunks.st: And he must give her half a kav of

chunks.st: And he must give her a bed,

chunks.st: a soft mat, and a hard mat.

chunks.st: And he must give her a cap for her head,

chunks.st: and a belt for her waist,

mishnayos.summary: The husband also gives his wife pocket money, and she eats with him on Friday nights. In return, she spins a set amount of wool for him; a richer husband must give more.

chunks.en: He gives her a silver ma'ah for her needs,
chunks.st: he must give her another silver ma’a coin for the rest of her needs.

chunks.en: and she eats with him every Friday night.
chunks.st: And she eats with him from Shabbat evening to Shabbat evening.

chunks.st: And if he does not give her a

chunks.st: silver ma’a coin for her needs,

chunks.en: And if she was nursing a baby,

chunks.en: But for an important man,

mishnayos.summary: What a wife finds and what she earns belong to her husband, and he eats the fruits of what she inherits. Payments for her shame and damage are hers, and Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says the husband gets a share.

chunks.st: object found by a wife and the wife’s earnings belong

chunks.st: to her husband. And with regard to her inheritance,

chunks.st: the husband enjoys the profits of this property in her lifetime.

mishnayos.summary: A man promised money to his son-in-law, and the son-in-law died. The Sages say he may tell the brother who marries the widow, I wanted to give it to your brother, not to you.

mishnayos.summary: When a kallah brings money or goods into the marriage, the chasan writes a bigger amount in the kesubah for money and a smaller amount for goods. Goods were usually valued at more than they were really worth.

chunks.st: pledged to bring in for him one thousand dinars in cash as a dowry,

mishnayos.summary: A father who marries off his daughter must give her at least fifty zuz. A chasan must dress his kallah before she leaves her father's house, and the tzedakah fund helps an orphan girl get married.

chunks.en: One who marries off his daughter without saying how much,

chunks.en: must not give her less than fifty zuz.
chunks.st: he must not give her less than fifty dinars.
